text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for release v2.14.0 -> 5% prod-us-east-1. canary_id=canary-20260315T1200 :rocket:
Olivia: heads up — I just opened the healthcheck dashboard, seeing a rising 5xx trend in the canary. hitting abort threshold?
Mira: pinging oncall... @Sam are you available?
Sam: oncall here, looking now. pulling logs and health metrics.
metrics-bot: healthcheck 5xx_rate: 4.2% (threshold=3.0%) window=5m region=prod-us-east-1
Sam: confirmed — abort criteria reached. preparing to trigger canary kill-switch.
Sam: will toggle feature flag and start rollback if kill succeeds. calling out to release-bypass flow.
Olivia: tagging as potential customer impact, please update CS if we flip.
Sam: executing kill: `POST https://internal-api/release/kill` payload: `{\"canary_id\":\"canary-20260315T1200\"}`
deploy-bot: kill request accepted -> 200 OK. feature flag `release.v2_14_canary` set to `off` :white_check_mark:
Jordan: saw traffic shift back to baseline pools, pods scaling down for canary.
Sam: initiating rollback to stable image stable-20260228. command: `deployctl rollback --id canary-20260315T1200 --to stable-20260228`
deploy-bot: rollback job queued. 3 canary pods terminating, stable pods replacing.
Mira: quick customer-impact check: edge logs show a tiny uptick in user 5xxs ~0.015% global, concentrated in us-east-1 between 12:11-12:14 UTC. no CS tickets yet.
Olivia: okay, minimal customer impact but we should create an incident and do a short postmortem. severity P2?
Sam: agree P2. creating INC-9876 now. incident-bot: created INC-9876 "Canary v2.14.0 healthcheck 5xx -> abort" assigned to Sam.
Sam: pasting short audit/log snapshot for handoff:
```
[12:05:31 UTC] deploy-bot: canary canary-20260315T1200 started -> 5%
[12:11:02 UTC] metrics-bot: healthcheck 5xx_rate 3.1%
[12:12:36 UTC] metrics-bot: healthcheck 5xx_rate 4.2% -> abort threshold crossed
[12:13:10 UTC] Sam: POST /release/kill -> 200 OK
[12:13:45 UTC] deployctl: rollback to stable-20260228 initiated
[12:15:02 UTC] deploy-bot: canary pods terminated, traffic reverted
```
Jordan: thanks — grabbing the rest of the logs and will keep an eye overnight. any suspected root cause?
Sam: initial grep points to tokenizer upgrade in v0.8.2 used by the canary model. stack traces show NPE in tokenization step under specific prompt shapes. not consistent with baseline.
Olivia: please add that to INC-9876 description and cc Eng-ML. Mira, can you notify CS for the top 10 affected accounts in us-east? mention we're proactively monitoring.
Mira: on it. Sending email to CS leads and pasting notes in the ticket.
Sam: handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. @Jordan you'll take night oncall for this incident — escalation policy remains PAGERDUTY PROD_ONCALL -> Eng-ML on second page. If 5xx resurges >2% for 10m, escalate immediately.
Jordan: ack. I'll run canary sanity checks repeatedly and watch for any reappearance, will also schedule a canary reproduction test against tokenizer v0.8.2 tomorrow.
Sam: leaving note: do not re-run v2.14 canary until Eng-ML confirms tokenizer patch or we pin tokenizer to v0.8.1.
Olivia: good call. add a pre-rollout test that includes short prompt sequences that previously triggered the NPE.
incident-bot: INC-9876 updated: Severity=P2, Owner=Sam, Status=investigating.
Mira: CS notified top accounts; no customer replies yet.
Jordan: taking over monitoring. will update timeline and ping if anything changes.
Sam: thanks team — closing this thread for now, will postmortem draft in INC-9876 and link to this thread. :folded_hands:
